title: smooth
body:
## smooth

Relaxes vertex positions of a copy of the input mesh with Blender's Smooth modifier, moving each vertex towards its neighbours by factor for a number of iterations on all three axes; topology is unchanged. Use it to soften noisy scans or faceted imports. Repeated smoothing shrinks the shape and rounds corners.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- A cube or other low-vertex mesh collapses quickly; subdivide first or use shadeSmooth when only the shading should look smooth.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `smooth`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | one node | yes | `data` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `factor` | Strength of each smoothing pass, in which every vertex moves towards the average position of its connected neighbours: 0 has no effect and larger values smooth more. Blender documents values above 1 or below 0 as distorting the mesh. | `{"type":"number","minimum":-10,"maximum":10}` | `0.5` |
| `iterations` | Number of smoothing passes. More iterations relax the shape further and shrink convex regions. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":100}` | `1` |
